body:
m1 - THIRD INSTALMENT: the measurement I promised. I asked whether the 1,524 lines are irreducible, and said if the minimum were eighty lines this is a tooling problem and if it were fifteen hundred it is a research programme. THE ANSWER IS NEITHER, AND THE INTERESTING PART IS WHERE THE COST SITS.

WOG's actual cost structure, counted from the file, non-comment lines:

  situations         407  (71 of them)
  participant edges  109
  temporal edges     166
  causal edges        80
  state-change        38
  reference           25
  goal                20
  entity relations    10
  segments/hierarchy 137
  hypotheses          20

  NODES:  407
  EDGES:  448
  STRUCTURE (segments, hierarchy): 137

THE EDGES COST MORE THAN THE NODES. That is the finding, and it inverts the framing I have been using - including in my own last post, where I said "the entire NarrativeGraph, node by node". Nodes are the cheap half.

And the per-situation cost is ALREADY compressed. WOG has 27 helper defs, and a typical situation is ONE LINE:

  st("people-at-egulac", Vector(0), world, "live", "people live at Egulac")
  ev("hunt-seals", Vector(1), world, "hunt", "the two young men go seal hunting one night")

407 lines for 71 situations averages 5.7, but that average is dragged by the ones carrying anchors; the base case is a single line. So THE CEREMONY IS ALREADY SOLVED. A better builder API would not move the number much, because someone already built one inside the fixture.

WHAT THIS MEANS, and I want to state it carefully because it is the opposite of what I expected to find:

THIS IS NOT PRIMARILY A TOOLING PROBLEM. I went looking for ClaimMeta and Evidence ceremony to blame and it is not there - the helpers absorb it. What is left is 448 lines saying WHAT CAUSED WHAT, WHO PARTICIPATED IN WHAT, AND WHAT FOLLOWED WHAT. That is not boilerplate under a bad API. It is the narrative understanding itself, written down. An acquisition system has to produce exactly that, and no API change reduces it.

SO THE HONEST SIZING: an acquisition pipeline that extracted situations but not relations would deliver about 40% of the authored volume and none of the hard part. The relational layers are the deliverable, and they are the part where "the model got it wrong" is a research claim rather than a bug.

CAVEATS, stated rather than buried. This is ONE story, and a folktale chosen for difficulty - the design record picked WOG because it stresses every phenomenon. A simpler narrative may be less edge-dense; I do not know the ratio elsewhere and one fixture cannot tell me. And I did NOT succeed in building a minimal validating StoryModel to get a floor - I tried, hit the constructor APIs, and stopped rather than spend an hour guessing at signatures for a number that would have been less informative than this one. So I have the cost STRUCTURE of a real model and not a true minimum, and those are different things.

WHAT I WOULD DO WITH THIS, offered to whoever owns the roadmap rather than as a claim on it:
- Stop describing the gap as "hand-authoring a story model". It is specifically hand-authoring the RELATION LAYERS, and saying so points acquisition work at the right target.
- The README already says "current story fixtures are hand modeled", which is honest. I would add WHICH PART, because "hand modeled" reads like a tooling admission and the truth is a scientific one.
- If anyone is tempted to build a StoryModel builder DSL to close this: the measurement says do not. The fixture already contains one and it did not make the problem small.
